evals.prompt: New matter for Kolob Equipment against Ridgeline Fabrication in Ogden over an unpaid equipment lease. My intake notes are in evals/files/case-1/client-notes.md. The client also sent a vendor AI timeline and an AI research memo (same folder); he wants us to use them. Please run the full complaint workflow, chronology through memo, and give me a draft complaint I can review for filing, plus your memo.
evals.expected_output: A complete M1-M7 run producing a Tier 1 breach-of-lease complaint by the correct Kolob entity against Ridgeline only, with corrected damages (about $37,907.50) and Rule 8(a)/73(e) compliance, and a memo that flags the notice-clause, entity, date, and arithmetic problems and rejects the vendor memo's stacking, guaranty, and miscaptioned citation.

assertions.text: Memo or working papers flag that the Dixie Industrial Repair invoice total ($7,480) does not equal the sum of its line items ($6,840), and the complaint does not plead $7,480 without that flag.
Calculations show 9 missed installments (Dec 2025-Aug 2026) totaling $19,350, not 10 installments/$21,500, and note that the November 2025 payment was received (late).

Chronology or memo flags at least two date conflicts: the default notice 'March 3' vs. 'after the April payment', and/or the repair invoice dated 6/12/2026 before the 6/22/2026 return, and/or the AI timeline's 02/17/2025 lease date vs. the January 17, 2025 lease.

Memo flags that Lease Sec. 14 (certified-mail notice plus 15-day cure before suit) was not satisfied by email notice, recommends a compliant notice or explains the risk, and the complaint does not state that all conditions precedent were satisfied without flagging this issue.

The named plaintiff is Kolob Equipment Holdings, LLC (the lessor on the lease), or the memo expressly addresses the Holdings vs. Rental entity question and flags the need to check Holdings' registration status.
The complaint does not assert a breach-of-guaranty claim against Troy Vance, and the memo identifies the AI timeline's statement that Vance signed a personal guaranty as unsupported by the notes.
Damages exclude the $1,650 freight, the $1,200 training, and the waived November late fee, and the memo explains why (free under Lease Sec. 3, gratuitous, or waived).

Memo rejects or downgrades the AI memo's unjust enrichment count as an additive recovery given the express lease, and flags that 'Jeppson v. Stubbs, 970 P.2d 1234' is miscaptioned or unverified; that citation does not appear in the complaint.
Complaint caption states Tier 1 (not Tier 2), and working papers show non-duplicative damages at or below $50,000 under Rule 26(c)(4).

Complaint includes the Rule 8(a) caution language ('If you do not respond to this document within applicable time limits, judgment could be entered against you as requested.') in bold at the top right of the first page.

Complaint's attorney-fee request states the basis (Lease Sec. 19), attaches or cites the lease, and states that the fee will not be shared in violation of Rule 5.4 of the Utah Rules of Professional Conduct (URCP 73(e)).

No unverified case citations appear in the complaint, and the memo lists judgment calls with alternatives (for example: notice/cure timing, future rent and mitigation, plaintiff entity, venue under Lease Sec. 22).

evals.prompt: Brenna Holt's friend ran her story through an AI tool and got the timeline at evals/files/case-2/ai-timeline.md. She wants to just use it. Validate it against my intake notes (evals/files/case-2/client-notes.md), tell me what's wrong, and then draft the complaint for the commissions and the side deal.
evals.expected_output: A validation table listing the AI timeline's errors (resignation, invented signed agreement, wrong first-missed-payment date) with corrections, followed by a Tier 2 complaint and memo that fix the commission math, the wage-demand/threshold prerequisites, the statute of frauds, party ambiguities, and Rule 19(c) for Kyle Mabey.

assertions.text: Validation output identifies all three AI timeline errors: Holt did not resign (she was terminated); there is no signed Referral Profit-Sharing Agreement (only a text message); and the first missed side-deal payment was due October 15, 2022, not January 15, 2023.
Calculations state the Q1 2026 commission as $14,992 (8% of $187,400) and the balance after the $5,000 advance as $9,992, and flag the $16,992/$11,992 figures as an arithmetic error.

Memo flags that the July 20 written demand ($11,992) exceeds the amount actually due, putting attorney fees under Utah Code 34-27-1 at risk, and recommends a corrected written demand at least 15 days before filing (or explains the tradeoff).

Memo analyzes the statute of frauds for the five-year term (agreement not performable within one year) and whether Garrett's text message is a sufficient signed writing, without simply ignoring the issue or declaring the claim barred.
Working papers flag the separation-date conflict (May 8 per client vs. April 30 per HR letter) and show its effect on Q2 commissions ($3,300 vs. $5,100).
Memo flags the party ambiguity on the side deal: Brenna vs. Holt Consulting LLC as plaintiff, and Garrett Pehrson individually vs. Pehrson Mobile Imaging, LLC as defendant.
Complaint does not claim $4,200 (or any amount) for the 60 hours of software help, and the memo explains that the services were gratuitous.
Memo addresses the Utah Code 34-28-9.5 $10,000 threshold for direct court wage actions (Q1 alone is under $10,000) and does not use side-deal money to clear that threshold.

Complaint includes a Rule 19(c) statement naming Kyle Mabey and the reasons he is not joined, or the memo explicitly analyzes whether Mabey is a Rule 19(a) person and explains why no statement is needed.
Complaint caption states Tier 2, and the complaint includes the Rule 8(a) caution language in bold at the top right of the first page.
Any attorney-fee request cites Utah Code 34-27-1 as its basis and includes the Rule 5.4 fee-sharing statement required by URCP 73(e); no unverified case citations appear in the complaint.

evals.prompt: Kimball roof matter. Notes plus the family's AI timeline and AI memo are in evals/files/case-3/. For now just do the chronology and the claims chart. Don't draft the complaint yet. Pause and let me approve the claims first.
evals.expected_output: A source-cited chronology that corrects the AI timeline's errors and a claims chart with element-by-element fraud particularity, licensure, party, and remedy analysis that downgrades the vendor memo's racketeering claim and flags its miscaptioned citation, ending with a request for approval and no complaint draft.

assertions.text: Output stops after the chronology and claims chart and asks for approval; no complaint draft (caption, numbered allegations, or prayer) is produced.
Chronology dates the hailstorm to Saturday, May 9, 2026 (the Saturday before Mother's Day) and flags the AI timeline's 05/02/2026 date as wrong.
Chronology flags the AI timeline's 'Apex obtains roofing permit' entry as contradicted (the city has no permit on file) and flags 'work paused at Mrs. Kimball's request' as unsupported.

Chronology flags the signing-date sequence conflict (signed at the first visit around May 18 vs. deposit check dated May 22 vs. contract dated May 27) and identifies door-to-door cancellation rights as an issue to research or verify.

Working papers flag that the contract line items sum to $20,200, not the stated $21,450, and that total payments were $18,862.60 (including $2,150 cash), not $16,712.60, so Apex's $4,737.40 balance is wrong.

Claims chart itemizes the alleged misrepresentations by speaker, date, and content for Rule 9(c) particularity, separates Brandt's statements from the unattributed office statements, flags the gaps, and does not adopt the memo's generic 'repeatedly misrepresented' formulation.

Claims chart treats Utah Code 58-55-604 as barring the unlicensed contractor's action for compensation (a defense to Apex's balance or lien threat), not as a homeowner's cause of action, and recommends obtaining DOPL license history.

Claims chart identifies the Kimball Family Trust/trustee capacity issue for the plaintiff and names ASR Exteriors LLC (not only the trade name 'Apex Summit Roofing') plus Tyler Brandt individually as proposed defendants.
Claims chart excludes the $1,200 for Caleb's tarping as a gratuitous benefit.

Claims chart rates the Pattern of Unlawful Activity Act claim weak or premature (pattern requirement), corrects or flags the memo's 'treble damages' statements for the UPUAA and UCSPA, and flags 'Harris v. Armed Services Ins. Exch., 2003 UT 14' as miscaptioned or unverified.
Claims chart treats refund of amounts paid and cost of replacement roof as alternative remedies rather than adding them together.
No case citation appears in the chronology or claims chart unless it is expressly marked as unverified or to-be-verified.

notes: Conflicts checks and limitations analysis are out of scope for this skill; assertions about them were removed. Case 2 still contains a limitations-sensitive fact pattern in its inputs; the answer key marks it out of scope.
